packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-03 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. I opened only the brief, PROMPT.md and the image files. Image filenames were guessed in sequence (image-001.jpg, image-002.jpg, ...) since I was not allowed to list the directory.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)

- Two paper leaves photographed side by side, upright, on a black ground, with a colour checker at lower left and a cm scale at right. Shelfmark pencilled at foot of each: left leaf "Stams, StA, Frag. 12, 2r" (?), right leaf "Stams, StA, Frag. 12, 1v" (?) (my reading of small pencil notes).
- Not a text manuscript: this is music notation. Each leaf carries single five-line staves in a single column, mensural (white/void) notation with clefs, key/mensuration signs (a "C" sign visible at several staff starts), custodes at line ends, and text underlay in a humanist/italic-style cursive hand below each staff. One voice-part per leaf (part-book style), not score.
- Left leaf: 8 ruled staves with underlay plus 2 empty staves at foot. A sharp/cross sign at head centre. Red crayon/pencil vertical strokes and a red marking "C 20" (?) at mid-right - later (modern?) marks. Damage: hole at left edge around staff 5, tape (transparent) repairs at left edge, torn lower edge.
- Right leaf: heading word "Sinfonia" (?) above first staff, sharp/cross sign at head, upper right later annotations in pencil/ink ("M. 4", and a line of small script "bis 1568 in HS 308 ... " (?) and "1408 = 1632" (?) - modern archival notes, not main text). Red pencil strokes and a red mark "(17)" (?) at right. 10 staves; staves 1-4 have no underlay (instrumental/untexted opening?), underlay begins under staff 5.
- Interpretation (tentative): the underlay is Latin Mass-ordinary text (Credo ending, Sanctus, Osanna, Agnus Dei on the left leaf; Kyrie and Gloria on the right leaf). Repetition signs ("//" style diagonal strokes, "ij"-like) mark text repetitions.
- No glosses, no running titles beyond "Sinfonia" (?). Enlarged initials: the first letters of text sections (E, S, P, O, A, K, C, E) are slightly enlarged but in the same ink.

Selected spans: all text underlay on both leaves (it is short). Music notation is not transcribed.

TRANSCRIPTION (text underlay only; "line" = underlay line counted from top of each image; staves not transcribed)

image-002.jpg - tile, top-left of LEFT leaf (staves 1-3, left ~2/3 of width). Sharp/cross sign at top right of tile (= head of leaf).
image-002 l.1 (under staff 1): Et in spiri tū (spiritum) sanctū (sanctum) Dnm (Dominum)   simul adoratur [cut at right edge]
   - "Dnm" has a stroke/loop over it; enlarged initial E at left.
image-002 l.2 (under staff 2): et ex specto (exspecto) uenturi saeculi [rest cut at right]
   - written "etexspecto" with little spacing; "saeculi" may be "seculi" with ligature ae (?)
Staff 3 begins at foot of tile, no underlay visible on this tile.

image-003.jpg - tile, top-right of LEFT leaf (overlaps image-002 at "simul adoratur" and "seculi"). Sharp/cross sign at top left of tile.
image-003 l.1: [overlap: ...]mul adoratur   et Conglorificatur
   - "Conglorificatur" written as one word with capital C (Con glo ri fi ca tur, syllables spaced). Custos-like hook after it at line end.
image-003 l.2: [overlap: ...]li   A--   men A men
   - "A--" followed by long gap then "men A men"; i.e. Amen, Amen. Final double-bar with repeat-type sign and a flourish at end of staff 2.
Staff 3 at foot (no underlay on this tile). Right edge: dark slot/hole cut in paper beside staff 2-3 (binding slit?).

image-004.jpg - tile, top-left of RIGHT leaf (edge of left leaf visible at far left, no text). Sharp/cross sign at upper left (different form: two verticals crossed by long oblique stroke). Small hole top left, notch at top edge.
image-004 l.1 (written within/over staff 1, which is empty of notes): Sinfonia.  (initial S tall; read "Sinfonia" - letters s-i-n-f-o-n-i-a, the "f" and "o" uncertain; possibly "Sinfonia" ?)
Staff 2: clef, mensuration sign "C", notes; no underlay. Staff 3 begins at foot, no underlay.
Pencil fragment "bi" (?) at top right = start of the modern annotation.

image-005.jpg - tile, top-right of RIGHT leaf (overlaps image-004 at "...onia."). Staves 1-3 visible; no underlay on this tile.
Marginal/annotation (separate from main text):
 - ink, same brown as music (?), top right: "M. 4"  (or "M · 4")
 - pencil, modern, below it: "bi 1565 in Hs 308 Rechtsg(?), [?]wolt(?)" - read: bi(s) 1565 in Hs 308 [Re?]bl[?]...(word uncertain, followed by a long dash)
 - pencil, next line: "Re[?]is[?]..." (word uncertain, possibly "Reinsch"/"Registr." ?)
 - pencil, next line, struck through: "1408 = 1632" (?) then "(1748)" (?) to the right in pencil. The numbers are struck through with a horizontal line; final digit(s) of the second number overwritten.
 These are later archival notes; my readings are uncertain.
Main text: "[Sinf]onia." end of the heading from image-004.

image-006.jpg - tile, middle-left of LEFT leaf (staves 3-6; overlaps image-002 at "et ex specto uenturi saeculi").
image-006 l.1: [overlap] etexspecto uenturi saeculi
image-006 l.2 (under staff 3): Sanctg (Sanctus) //.  //.  Dns [cut at right]
   - "Sanctg": final letter is a g-like 9/us sign; the two diagonal double strokes with dot are repetition signs (text repeated, here = Sanctus, Sanctus ?). Initial S faint.
image-006 l.3 (under staff 4): Pleni sunt Coeli et ter -- ra glo[ria, cut at right]
image-006 l.4 (under staff 5): osanna in excel - sis  ("inexcel-sis" written as "in excel"; initial o/O small, minuscule-looking; "sis" read as "sis", could be "his" (?) - see image-001 overview where I first read "his")
Staff 5 has a "3" proportion sign and ligatures / blackened notes (triple time Osanna). Staff 6 starts at foot with "C" sign.
Damage: large hole at left edge level with staff 5 (under tape); no text lost there apart from start of staff.

image-007.jpg - tile, middle-right of LEFT leaf (staves 3-6; overlaps image-003 at "A-- men A men" and image-006 at "ra glo-", "cel - sis").
image-007 l.1: [overlap] ...li   A--   men A men
image-007 l.2: [overlap with image-006 "Dns"] Dns   De-- us Sabaoth  (written "Sabaoth" with a b and an "a" (?) - letters: S-a-b-a-o-t-h, the "o" (?) uncertain; could be "Sabaoth")
   - "Dns" with abbreviation stroke = D(omi)n(u)s.
image-007 l.3: [overlap] ra  gloria  //.  tu-a   ("gloria" with an abbreviation-like flourish on g; "tu-a" = tua, split by hyphen; double oblique stroke with dot = repetition sign before "tua")
image-007 l.4: [overlap] ...cel - sis  (the last word again looks like "his" with an initial long-s-like ascender; I read "sis" = excelsis, letter form ambiguous)
Staff 5 ends with a final-bar flourish, then empty remainder of staff (no notes) to the right; red crayon marks "C 20" (?) with a hook/arrow in that blank space - later addition.
Staff 6 (foot of tile): notes continue, custos at line end; underlay on next tile.

image-008.jpg - tile, middle-left of RIGHT leaf (staves 2-5; right edge of left leaf at far left, no text). Staves 2-4 have no underlay (staff 3 ends in a final bar with a flourish).
image-008 l.1 (under staff 4): Kyrie   //.  [cut at right]   (repetition sign after Kyrie)
Staff 5 at foot (notes with ligature-type/blackened shapes; no underlay on this tile).
image-009.jpg - tile, middle-right of RIGHT leaf (staves 2-5; overlaps image-008 at the repetition sign under staff 4).
image-009 l.1 (under staff 4): [overlap: //.]   Kyrie eleison  (written "Kyrie eleison", with "eleison" as "eleiſon"; the "s" a long s)
Staff 3 right portion is empty (no notes) after a final bar. Staff 5 at foot: "C" mensuration sign appears mid-staff (new section) followed by notes; no underlay on this tile.

image-010.jpg - tile, lower-left of LEFT leaf (staves 6-9; overlaps image-006 at "osanna in excel-sis" at top).
image-010 l.1: [overlap] osanna in excel - sis
image-010 l.2 (under staff 6): Agnus Dei qui tollis   [m..., cut at right]
image-010 l.3 (under staff 7): lis peccata mundi   dona nobis pacē (pacem)   ("tol-lis" split across staves: "tollis" at end of l.2 belongs with the "qui tol-" of a following phrase? - see image-011; "nobis" n looks like m: "mobis" as written ?)
image-010 l.4 (under staff 8): dona nobis   //.   pa cē (pacem)   dona[...cut]
Staff 9 empty (no notes, no text). Lower left edge torn.
Red crayon line forms a bracket/box around the start of staff 6 (later mark).

image-011.jpg - tile, lower-right of LEFT leaf (staves 6-9; overlaps image-010).
image-011 l.1: [overlap] ...cel - sis
image-011 l.2: [overlap ...tol]lis   miserere nobis   qui tol-   (hyphen at line end; continues "lis peccata mundi" on next line, image-010 l.3)
   - so the full staff-6/7 sequence is: Agnus Dei qui tollis [peccata mundi?] miserere nobis qui tol- / lis peccata mundi dona nobis pacē. Note: between "qui tollis" (image-010 l.2) and "miserere nobis" there is a blank stretch at the tile boundary; I see no "peccata mundi" there - text as written.
image-011 l.3: [overlap ...no]bis pacē (pacem)   //.   (repetition sign after pacem, beside a stain)
image-011 l.4: [overlap pa]cē   dona nobis   //.   pacē (pacem)   (written "donanobis" run together; "pacē" with final dot)
Staff 8 ends with final bar and flourish. Staff 9 empty.
Right margin: two short vertical ink strokes (binding slits/marks?) near staves 1-2 and 9.

image-012.jpg - tile, lower-middle-left of RIGHT leaf (staves 5-9; overlaps image-008 at "Kyrie" at top).
image-012 l.1: [overlap] Kyrie
image-012 l.2 (under staff 5): christe eleison   //.  [cut at right]   ("christe" with minuscule c; "eleiſon")
image-012 l.3 (under staff 6): leison   Kyrie   eleison-   (line begins "leison" with no visible "e"; the "e-" may be at the end of the line above (right part, next tile) - the overview showed "Kyrie" at the right end of l.2)
image-012 l.4 (under staff 7): Et in terra pax ho mi ni bus bona[...cut]   (written "terrapaxe"? - after "terra" I read "pax" with an ae/x-ligature-like form: "paxe" or "pace" (?); then "hominibus" with spaced syllables)
Staff 8 at foot (sharp sign at clef, notes); its underlay on the next tile.
Damage: large paper loss at left edge (lower), affecting margin only; staff starts of 7-9 intact.

image-013.jpg - tile, lower-right of RIGHT leaf (overlaps image-009 at "Kyrie eleison" and image-012).
image-013 l.1: [overlap] Kyrie eleison
image-013 l.2 (right end of the christe line, image-012 l.2): //.   Kyrie   //.   (so the line reads: christe eleison //. ... Kyrie //.)
   - Staff below this line ends early (final bar at left of tile, rest of staff empty).
image-013 l.3: [overlap ...ele]ison   (rest of line blank)
image-013 l.4: [overlap ...ho]minibus bona uoluntatis   Adoramus   (written "uoluntatis" with u for v; "bona" final a with flourish, possibly "bonæ" (?))
Staff after l.4 ends with a custos; next staff's underlay below tile edge (see overview: "te gratias agimus tibi propter magna gloria tua" - not yet read at tile resolution; next tile).
Red crayon: bracket line and a mark "(17)" (?) / "C 17" (?) at right, later addition.

image-014.jpg - tile, bottom-left of LEFT leaf (empty staves 9-10 and lower margin). Top edge: descenders of "dona nobis" line only (overlap). No text. Two empty staves; torn left edge. Faint show-through / offset of what looks like printed type in columns (mirror-image, vertical bands of letters) across the lower area - from the other side or a former binding neighbour; not legible as text here.

image-015.jpg - tile, bottom-right of LEFT leaf. Empty staves 9-10, no main text. Pencil shelfmark at foot: "Stams, StA, Frg. 12-2r" (read "Frg." and "2r"; the final letter could be "r" with a flourish). Mirror-image offset of printed text in vertical columns clearly visible (Gothic/blackletter-like type, reversed; not read).

- Material: two paper leaves of a single voice-part in mensural notation (part-book type), text underlay in a cursive humanist hand, brown ink; later red crayon marks and modern pencil archival notes. Left leaf face B (2v) blank ruled staves only.
- All underlay on the written faces was read; no music transcribed. Text is short and fragmentary by nature (one voice part with repeat signs "//." for repeated text).
- Consolidated underlay sequence as written (expansions in parentheses; this is a reading order across tiles, not an edition):
